extracted.intended_audience: social scientists and researchers who want to upload papers, preprints, data, or code to SocArXiv/OSF Preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and platform policies for submitting working papers, preprints, post-prints, and related research materials to the SocArXiv (OSF Preprints) repository, including moderation, licensing, versioning, and withdrawal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly and minimally informative/complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be scholarly (as well as minimally informative and complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation confirms submissions are scholarly and provide enough information to be meaningful to readers. This is the first item on the moderation checklist; moderation is expected to take less than two days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Within supported research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be in research areas that SocArXiv supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation checks that the subject matter falls within the repository’s supported disciplines and topical scope; consult the moderation policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausible categorization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should select appropriate categories/metadata so moderators and readers can understand the paper’s disciplinary placement; implausible or misleading category choices may be flagged during moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fraudulent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators screen for obvious fraud (e.g., fabricated content, fake authorship); submissions suspected of fraud may be rejected or removed per the moderation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct attribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure author names and contributor metadata are accurate. Moderation checks for correct attribution; misattribution can cause rejection or require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted languages only
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be in languages that SocArXiv moderates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions in unsupported languages may be rejected. Check the moderation policy for which languages are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-searchable file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in text-searchable formats (such as PDF or docx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a text-searchable file so content can be indexed and searched; scanned images or non-searchable formats may be rejected or requested to be re-uploaded in an acceptable format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author right to share
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv seeks to accept only papers that authors have the right to share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the moderation process does not check copyrights, authors should only upload versions they are permitted to distribute. If a copyright claim is substantiated post-upload, SocArXiv may be obliged to remove the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: New versions subject to moderation (policy change from 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in 2025, new versions of papers are subject to moderation as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you upload a revised version, it will go through the moderation checklist before it appears. Plan for moderation delay for updates and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working paper eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Working papers: any draft of a paper that is ready to share with interested parties but has not yet been peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal for drafts you want to widen beyond colleagues, conference audiences, or journal submission circles. SocArXiv hosts working papers at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints: typically completed papers that have not yet been peer reviewed (but definitions vary and can include accepted-but-not-yet-published versions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SocArXiv will host preprints regardless of whether the term is interpreted narrowly (unrefereed drafts) or more broadly (accepted manuscripts awaiting publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-print (author-archived/publisher-allowed) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-prints: versions of a paper shared after journal publication (may be author’s version without publisher formatting or the publisher’s version if you have the right to distribute it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this option to make published work accessible if it’s behind a paywall and you have permission to share the publisher’s version or an allowable author’s manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: License selection and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv offers license options: No license, CC-0 1.0 Universal (public domain waiver), or CC-BY Attribution 4.0 International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC-0 donates work to the public domain (no permission required). CC-BY lets authors keep copyright while requiring attribution and a link to license terms. Both CC options permit reuse, adaptation, distribution (including commercially) and promote openness and reuse certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach data, code, and research materials via OSF Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper on SocArXiv is automatically associated with a Project on the Open Science Framework platform; researchers can attach data, code, or other research materials to that project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the associated OSF Project to upload and link supplementary materials. The FAQ encourages sharing data and code to support openness and transparency; see the how-to guide for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check journal/publisher preprint/self-archiving policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether a specific journal permits sharing preprints or post-prints (most publishers permit sharing preprints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAQ notes that many journals permit preprints (e.g., ASA explicitly permits repository posting). Use journal websites, compiled lists, or tools like Open Policy Finder to check publisher copyright and self-archiving policies before uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOI and persistent URL assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers uploaded to SocArXiv/OSF Preprints receive a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and a persistent URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper already has a DOI from a publisher, that information can be included to link to the published version. OSF also creates a persistent URL for each paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account requirement (OSF account)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must create a free account on the Open Science Framework (OSF) as part of the upload process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click 'Add a Preprint' on SocArXiv.org and follow instructions; account creation is required to manage uploads and associated projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and correction workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: To correct a paper, post a new version; older versions remain available in version history while the newest version is served to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you no longer stand behind a paper, post a new version that announces the paper as withdrawn (older versions will still be visible in the history). New versions (from 2025) are moderated before display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy (limited removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, papers cannot be withdrawn once accepted unless there is a legal obligation (e.g., private personal information or a substantiated copyright claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If removal is required for legal reasons SocArXiv may remove the paper. Otherwise, the recommended approach is to post a corrected or withdrawn-version; version history preserves older copies.
